text:
tina: Quick blocker on docs PR #2602 -- the migration guide mentions automatic model fallback (for latency/capacity) but doesn't say how billing is attributed. Reviewers flagged this as a legal/product question.

rafael: good catch. we need explicit wording. what's the current runtime behavior?

kim: runtime clarification: billing is attributed to the model that actually served the request (the served_model). The response metadata includes both `requested_model` and `served_model`. For Hosted customers this is used to compute charges. For Dedicated customers on reserved capacity we charge against their commit band and not per-token billing; however metrics still record `served_model` for observability.

tina: ok, so docs should state that. A follow-up: if a request asks for `r-large` but falls back to `r-small-quant` mid-stream (fallback after partial tokens), how do we bill partial tokens?

kim: short answer: billing is per-token based on the model that emitted each token. If fallback happens mid-generation, tokens already emitted are billed at the original model if they were produced by it; subsequent tokens are billed at the fallback model. We emit per-chunk metadata indicating `chunk_model` where possible.

rafael: please confirm how this shows up in the API response for users who need audits. We need examples for docs showing fields to inspect.

kim: we include a `meta` block on the final response (and incremental stream events when streaming) with keys: `requested_model`, `served_model`, and `served_model_breakdown` when multiple models were used (list of {model, tokens}). Example (non-exhaustive) in docs: `{"requested_model":"r-large","served_model":"r-small-quant","served_model_breakdown":[{"model":"r-large","tokens":42},{"model":"r-small-quant","tokens":18}]}`.

docs-reviewer-olga: perfect. also add a note about telemetry: `served_model_breakdown` is available in hosted logs and the SDK `response.meta` but may be limited for Dedicated fleets depending on telemetry level. Reviewers want an SDK snippet showing how to read `served_model_breakdown`.

tina: adding snippet to PR. draft JS snippet: ```javascript
// read served_model_breakdown from API response
const resp = await client.generate({model: 'r-large', input: '...'});
console.log(resp.meta.requested_model, resp.meta.served_model);
if (resp.meta.served_model_breakdown) {
  resp.meta.served_model_breakdown.forEach(b => {
    console.log(`${b.model}: ${b.tokens} tokens`);
  });
}
```

rafael: also need to cover pricing nuance: if a customer has Reserved Dedicated capacity with a committed GPU pool, and fallback uses a hosted cheaper model (edge case in hybrid routing), how is billing handled?

kim: hybrid routing: if a request is routed off dedicated pool to hosted because of capacity or model mismatch, billing depends on contract: generally Hosted billing rules apply when served by hosted infrastructure. For Dedicated customers with commitments, we try to avoid routing off-pool; if it happens, ops will tag those requests and we bill per-hosted pricing unless contract specifies otherwise. Ops/billing teams have a reconciliation pipeline that tags such cross-invoice events. We'll add a note and link to the billing FAQ.

billing-bot: billing-note: cross-infrastructure fallback incidents are rare. Any customer-visible charges will appear under Hosted usage if the request executed on hosted infra. We record both `tenant_scope` and `infrastructure_scope` in charge logs.

docs-reviewer-olga: add a short recommended wording: "Billing is based on the actual model and infrastructure that served the request. Inspect `response.meta.served_model` and `response.meta.infra` for auditing. If you must guarantee billing to a specific model, disable automatic fallback with `allow_fallback=false` in route config."

tina: good call. need to show the route config snippet to disable fallback in the migration guide. adding YAML snippet: ```yaml
routes:
  - name: chat-proxy
    model: r-large
    allow_fallback: false # do not automatically route to cheaper/compatible models
```

rafael: also request docs mention that disabling fallback may cause increased 429s or higher latency if the requested model is unavailable; product wants a small callout.

kim: will add: "Note: disabling fallback can increase throttling and latency; consider canarying this change."

ci-bot: docs-preview: linkcheck failed for /docs/billing/fallback because billing FAQ anchor changed.

tina: fixing link to billing FAQ and adding small parenthetical about dedicated commit reconciliation. Pushing update.

ci-bot: docs-preview: all checks passed. linter: flagged missing code fence language on JS snippet.

tina: updated fences. pushing final.

docs-reviewer-olga: re-reviewing. once we include the explicit `served_model_breakdown` example and the route `allow_fallback` note, I'll approve. Keep the billing language conservative.

tina: done. final commit pushed.

ci-bot: docs-preview: all checks passed.

docs-reviewer-olga: approved. merging when you're ready.

tina: merging now. thanks for the quick answers.

kim: runtime note: we will not change billing attribution behavior this release. Any change affects accounting and needs finance sign-off.
